entries.definition: Mostly refers to Sarah Longwell of the Bulwark, often alongside JVL; chat suggests Destiny do a stream or collab with her.
Refers to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whom chat discussed alongside a news story about Nvidia and China.
Mostly part of diet pepsi or diet coke, a running joke about someone on stream wanting diet soda and lasagna.
Exasperation: posted at someone who said or did something dumb or annoying.
Agreement: posted after quoting or naming someone to say they are right, sometimes sarcastically next to COPIUM.
A strong-man face posted to approve of a bold or winning move; in these chats it sits next to wins, threats to opponents and RapThis spam.
"Simple as": posted after a blunt answer to say there's nothing more to it.
Hard laughter at something absurd, embarrassing or ironic.
A siren for urgent news: in these chats it flags new results, projections, needle moves and Polymarket swings.
A cheerful cat for liking something or calling it a W; often spammed in a row.
Marks a moment as great to watch: drama, a dramatic result, a collapse or a reveal.
Confused and lost: posted with "idgi" or when chat can't follow what's happening.
Disbelief or disgust at something said or shown.
Excitement or hype, also used for greetings and goodbyes.
Goofy shrugging: used with "idk", odd questions and offhand jokes.
Gloating at someone who just lost an argument or got dunked on; often paired with insults, SNARKED and SpeedLaugh.
Waiting for an answer: posted after a question to chat or the stream.
Bowing in respect to someone or something impressive, often spammed.
Teasing accusation: "I know what you are", posted at suggestive or suspicious lines.
Shock or outrage at something unforgivable or ridiculous, often spammed.
Suspicion: a side glance at something weird or at someone acting off.
Surprise or disbelief at something said or shown.
An alert bell for getting attention: chat puts it around breaking news, results to check and calls to look at something now.
Posted when someone is caught out saying or doing something, as a tease.
Paranoid or unhinged talk, posted with conspiratorial or rambling lines.
Taunting laughter at a loser, spammed in long rows; in these chats paired with insults at opponents.
A dancing celebration emote, spammed in rows; in these chats also around "vote" calls.
Nodding along: agreement with a claim or prediction, sometimes ironic.
A slow turtle: for slow loading or slow takes, sometimes spammed as a wall.
Hype for a win or a dunk, usually spammed with GIGACHAD.
Cozy contentment: feeling comfy or pleased.
Cope: refusing to accept bad news ("ITS NOT OVER COPIUM"), aimed at oneself or at others.
A dancing emote for vibing, usually spammed in a row.
Mock approval or resignation, tacked onto odd personal admissions and complaints.
A DGG heart: affection, congrats, greetings and birthday wishes.
Victory: in these chats the main emote for Democratic wins on election night 2026 ("BLUE WAVE").
Pointing up at what's on stream or what was just said, often with "holy".
Celebration: posted on good news for chat's side, such as an opponent losing or getting snarked.
A wave hello or goodbye.
Sad and annoyed at once; posted with complaints.
Excited pointing at something on screen.
"Let him cook": let someone finish their idea, often ironic when the idea is bad.
A running joke on stream about someone wanting or being denied diet pepsi, often paired with lasagna.
Mocking or hate-watching someone; chat used it for streamers and chatters going after each other in the Nov 2026 drama.
Chat discussed a news story about Nvidia chips reaching China and its politics.
Refers to Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer; chat is arguing over whether he and Hakeem Jeffries should keep their leadership roles.
Mockery aimed at a person or community, as in "snark him"; also the drama content itself ("such good snark").
Mostly appears in "cop slop", chat's label for cop-genre movies or shows, used with CINEMA and GODSTINY.
"Come on England": a mock-British cheer, used for urging something on.
Spiked with a news story about Nvidia chips and China that chat discussed, plus unrelated mentions.
Plotting: posted with schemes, tactics and someone being invited into a call.
Mocking goodbye to someone who lost or got banned.
Refers to the lobbying group AIPAC; chat mostly invokes it ironically or as a punchline when discussing who funds Democratic politicians.
Mild shock or a deadpan reaction.
"It's over": despair at bad news, a bad needle move or infighting.
Fights between streamers and community members; in Nov 2026 it meant an orbiter dispute over a meet-up, which chat followed for hours on stream.
An emote posted on its own when chat feels empty or quiet, for example after the stream ends.
"One guy": calling out that one person is behind something, or pointing at the one person who did it.
Text-to-speech donation messages read out on stream; chat comments on TTS being on, paused or left running.
A stream that a chatter has embedded on destiny.gg for others to watch; "top embed" is the most watched one and "ban the embed" asks for a stream to be pulled.
Used in chat's debate over the Democratic Party's congressional leadership after the 2026 election, mostly about Schumer and Jeffries.
A phone-call greeting ("hello"), used to get someone's attention or as a joke opener.
Part of a running joke on stream about someone wanting lasagna and diet pepsi.
Mostly refers to the movie Heat, which chat watched on stream; chat asks about a sequel and complains about missing it.
A person who follows a streamer mainly to mock them; chat throws the label at critics and at people it suspects of hate-watching.
Refers to House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, discussed alongside Schumer in chat's argument over Democratic leadership and the speaker race.
A political commentator chat is discussing because of his posts about Chuck Schumer and the Democratic congressional leadership fight.
Forced calm while things go badly ("WE HAVENT CALLED IT YET ItsFine"); often paired with COPIUM.
Name of a politician chat discusses as a possible Democratic Senate leader in place of Schumer, often posted with hype emotes.
Streams that chatters embed for others to watch in DGG chat; chat jokes about the embed rankings and about snarking at the embeds.
Used in talk about race realism and race science during the genetics segment; chat mostly mocks those arguments.
Computer memory; chat complains about RAM prices and jokes that Sam Altman and AI data centers are taking all of it.
Tow trucks and tow companies, which chat argues about during a talk on car breakdowns and roadside help.
An in-person event; in these chats mostly the election-night meetup around Destiny's stream and other streamer events chat compared it to.
Mostly refers to commentator Tim Pool; sometimes other people named Tim.
Plural of snarker: people who watch or follow someone mainly to mock them.
An emote spammed in bursts, usually on its own, sometimes alongside the word shoot.
Senator Jon Ossoff of Georgia; chat celebrated as his 2026 race against Mike Collins was called for him early on election night.
Mostly chat spamming that Destiny should check his Discord DMs, often with ALARMA.
Chat's name for cop movies or shows; chat asks for more of them to be watched on stream.
The 2026 Mississippi Senate race, which chat watched closely on election night as the NYT needle and Polymarket swung toward the Democrat; also spelled "mississipi".
Comes up in general talk about politics, AI content, bots spreading narratives and regulating social media.
During a stream segment on population genetics, dogs and dog breeds were the main analogy chat argued over, alongside wolves and selective breeding.
Coping with a loss; on election night 2026, "cope cam" meant putting the other side's reactions (for example Fox News) on stream.
Used for brown eyes in eye-color genetics talk, and appears in political names chat mentioned alongside election results.
An emote chat spams on its own, usually as a reaction to something said on stream.
Mostly in 'research stream', chat's name for long streams spent reading studies, here on genetics and race.
Car brakes; chat gives advice and jokes about a stuck brake and a brake rotor shown on stream.
Mostly part of "Chris Hansen", brought up around the movie Primetime; occasionally other Chrises.
The Texas races on election night 2026, mostly the Senate race; chat asked for updates, called it early and joked that Texas was blue ("blexas").
Short for Sam Altman, whom chat jokingly blames for buying up RAM and pushing up its price, and whose looks chat mocks.
An emote posted on its own or after someone's name, appears to be used as a peeking or lurking reaction.
In the Nov 2026 orbiter drama, chat argued over who made or didn't make plans to meet up, and whose fault it was.
Scott Colom, the Democrat in the 2026 Mississippi Senate race; chat tracked his vote lead and his odds on Polymarket.
Attention and status; "clout chaser" is the insult chat throws at people it thinks join drama for views.
Name of the tech executive chat jokingly blames for high RAM prices, and whose looks and speaking style chat mocks.
New batches of votes being reported ("BIG DUMPS"); chat asked for more of them in counties where its candidate needed votes.
Refers to the shared movie-night "theater"; chat jokes about the empty theater, fires in the theater and the new theater intro.
The 2026 Alaska races, mainly Peltola's; chat waited for the slow count to see if the Senate could reach 56.
A streamer or creator in Destiny's social circle who appears on or around his streams.
The prediction market chat checked for live odds on election night 2026, especially swings in the Mississippi race.
James Talarico, the Democrat in the 2026 Texas Senate race against Paxton; chat followed his lead all election night.
Used for a big target chat wants to take down, the "white whale", and for big-spending donors ("whale money").
Refers to the movie Primetime, which chat watched or wanted to watch during a movie night; chat posts reviews, scores and CINEMA hype about it.
Streamers and creators in Destiny's social circle; chat compares them and argues about how they treat DGG.
Refers to the decoys in the movie Primetime; chat spams lines about the decoy characters and jokingly calls chatters decoys.
Senator John Fetterman; in these chats, jokes about him switching parties and being the deciding vote.
Angie Nixon, a candidate chat followed on election night 2026 as her lead grew and then vanished.
Part of the Nov 2026 drama among Destiny's orbiters: chat argued over who was or was not invited to hang out during his election trip.
Mostly in 'Professor Dave', a creator chat brings up as someone who debunks videos like the one on stream.
Short videos the stream was scrolling through; chat reacts to and comments on them.
Refers to the movie The Odyssey, which chat says was shown during a movie night; chat is reviewing it and debating its casting.
Mostly part of "Chris Hansen". Chat brings him up in connection with the movie Primetime, asking what he thinks of it and comparing him to characters in it.
During a stream segment on population genetics, chat uses it for whether animals or groups can interbreed, often with the dogs-and-wolves example.
Short for developer; comes up in chat's talk about coding jobs, game dev, AI coding tools and getting a developer on stream to debate.
Lauren Boebert; on election night 2026 chat asked to check her race and posted that she was losing.
Refers to Chris Hansen, the TV host chat links to the movie Primetime; chat is asking for his take on the film and passing around his reported comments about it.
Used mostly about the movie Primetime and its predator-catching premise, with jokes like "predator team"; sometimes refers to the Predator film series.
Used in jokes about rewriting software from scratch, especially rewriting things in Rust or having AI rewrite them.
During a stream segment on population genetics, chat argues over what defines a species, using dogs and wolves as the main comparison.
Usually refers to actor Patrick Stewart, whose movies chat says it polled for movie night; sometimes other people named Stewart.
Used in theater-style jokes during movie viewings, with chat pretending to eat, share or spill popcorn.
Requests for a short summary of drama for people who just tuned in.
A panel discussion people in chat watched or took part in; chat reviews how it went and who did well.
The Browns NFL football team; chat reacts to a Browns game against the Saints.
Mostly refers to a video segment chat calls 'the academy' during a long reviewed video, plus mentions of Khan Academy; posted with CINEMA.
The roadside assistance membership; chat tells people to get AAA during a talk on car trouble and towing.
Appears to come from a political speech metaphor about a "red brick wall"; chat spams "RED BRICK WALL" with SCHIZO and debates what the metaphor meant.
Refers to UFC CEO Dana White. Chat is reacting, often with disbelief, to reports it was passing around that he was being considered for White House press secretary.
Used while watching a video game movie adaptation on stream; chat debates whether video game movies can be good.
Almost always part of "Dana White", the UFC CEO; chat is discussing reports it shared about him being offered the White House press secretary job.
During a stream segment on population genetics, chat uses it when discussing how genetic measures compare variation within and between human groups.
Saturday Night Live; chat is reacting to SNL skits shown on stream and asking for more or fewer of them.
Comes up in chat's argument over whether software developers deserve the title of engineers or are just code monkeys.
Part of Resident Evil, a movie chat watched on stream; chat reviews it and complains about missing it.
Comes up in chat's arguments about the average programmer, code quality and performance, and AI-written code.
During a stream segment on population genetics, chat uses it for which genes a study selected and what graphs of them show.
During a stream segment on population genetics, chat discussed selective breeding of dogs and whether interspecies offspring can reproduce.
Used in the dog-versus-wolf analogy chat argued about during the genetics segment, plus some jokey self-descriptions.
Chat's label for the person or arguments being reviewed in the race realism segment; chat mostly mocks them.
Used around the movie Primetime, which chat describes as being about catching predators; chat jokes about who the real predators in the story are.
Appears to be the title of a film or show chat was watching or discussing, plus jokes about the TV-studio meaning of a green room.
A nickname for Talarico that chat adopted from the other side and repeats with glee as he leads Paxton.
Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican in the 2026 Ohio governor race; chat cheered reports of his defeat.
Name for Richard Hanania, who appears to have come on or been shown on stream; chat reacts with jokes and argues about his politics.
Chat's word for the long population-genetics topic on stream; many lines complain about or joke about it.
Dog breeds, which chat compared using FST during the genetics segment.
The horror genre; chat discusses horror movies and survival horror games while watching a movie on stream.
Used in eye-color genetics talk for dominant versus recessive traits, often with brown eyes and GIGACHAD.
Mostly in 'fixation index', the genetic measure chat argued about; also used in joke pick-up lines about genes.
"Catching strays": getting criticized in passing when an argument was aimed at someone else.
Almost always part of 'race realism', chat's label for the stream segment debating race realist arguments.
The South Carolina Senate race, which chat flagged on election night 2026 when odds and early results looked close.
Chat's name for long streams spent reading and reacting to research, here on genetics.
Chat's label for the stream segment reviewing and debating race realist arguments, often called the 'race realism arc'; chat mostly mocks those arguments.
Code written by AI tools; chat argues over whether it is readable, buggy or maintainable compared with code written by people.
During a stream segment on population genetics, chat uses it for a specific version of a gene, mostly in talk about allele frequencies between populations.
Chanted in chat as part of mock socialist slogans like "honor and dignity" and "dignity for all".
During a stream segment on population genetics, chat compares wolves and dogs to argue about breeding and species boundaries.
Brandon Herrera, the Republican in a Texas House race (TX-23) that chat followed on election night 2026, comparing his fundraising and vote share.
Used for the allele frequency equation in the genetics segment, plus quadratic-equation and 'meme equation' jokes.
Almost always 'selective breeding', discussed with dog breeds in the genetics segment.
A name chat brings up while watching Primetime, joking that he should get his own movie or appear in a post-credit scene.
Appears to be FST, a genetic measure chat cites while arguing about how much populations or dog breeds differ genetically; chat debates what the number can and cannot show.
Almost always 'allele frequency' in the population-genetics segment.
Appears to come from 'Hardy-Weinberg', a genetics equation chat repeated and joked about during a population-genetics segment.
During a stream segment on population genetics, chat uses it for genetic differences within and between populations.
A running joke about a firepit (and a firepit meetup), usually posted with SCHIZO and laughing emotes, with chat suggesting the firepit never existed.
Refers to actor Robert Pattinson, whom chat praises while discussing his roles in movies watched or talked about during movie nights, including Primetime and The Odyssey.
Al Pacino, the actor; chat jokes about his role while watching Heat on stream.
Comes up in chat's arguments about whether programmers count as engineers and whether AI can do their work better.
A news channel that came up on stream; chat argued over whether it is the UK channel or Sky News Australia.
Chat explained and argued over what a gene is during the genetics segment, plus joke 'X gene' lines.
Chat's repeated request that the movie-night host or conductor show the movie Primetime.
How some chatters explained the Nov 2026 orbiter drama: a dispute that came from messages being misread or passed along.
A host chat watched in a discussion with Pete Buttigieg about voter ID; chat mostly criticizes PBD's arguments.
During a stream segment on population genetics, chat argues over whether the streamed argument implies human groups are different species, usually rejecting that idea.
Chat pleading with the streamer to play a clip, call or audio being discussed.
Used two ways: in genetics talk about whether pairings produce viable, fertile offspring, and appears to name a music act whose song titles chat posted.
A request to show the losing side's reaction on stream, such as Fox News coverage.
Comes up in chat's argument over whether AI-written code is readable, set against code written by people.
Misspelling of Mississippi: the 2026 Senate race between Colom and his opponent, which came down to a few thousand votes.
During a stream segment on population genetics, chat uses it for gene variants, often in eye-color and skin-color examples.
The AI company; chat discusses it next to Anthropic and Google, its models, its work on math problems, and AI lobbying and competition.
The grocery store chain; chat was talking about it while watching a video about Aldi on stream and comparing it to other grocers.
During a stream segment on population genetics, chat uses it alongside differentiation, variation and FST while arguing about group differences.
